findings_list.evidence: update_github_artifacts overwrites .github/workflows/ci.yml unconditionally on every `specboot update` with no fingerprint check and no backup (backup_framework_files iterates UPDATE_ITEMS, which does NOT include .github/workflows/ci.yml). This is asymmetric with the careful fingerprint-protected handling of release.yml (repair_legacy_release) and with REQ-001's 'custom workflows never touched' principle: a consumer that replaced ci.yml before adopting Specboot (or a non-framework ci.yml) would have it silently clobbered.
findings_list.recommendation: Fingerprint-gate the ci.yml overwrite (allowlist the consumer-ci.yml content) or back it up into .specboot-backup-<ts>/ before replacing; at minimum warn when the existing ci.yml differs from the framework template.

findings_list.evidence: repair_legacy_release: if the backup cp fails (stderr swallowed at line 782) or backup_dir is empty (--no-backup), rm -f (line 784) still removes the allowlisted legacy release.yml; recoverable from framework git history because content is blob-addressed in the allowlist. Confirmed unchanged in the current tree.
findings_list.recommendation: Abort or warn with higher severity when the backup of a framework-owned file fails before rm -f.

findings_list.evidence: mergedBlock keeps a global scalar permission as fallback after agent-map patterns (lines 115-126) and evaluateEffective (129-139) still applies that scalar fallback; if OpenCode's per-key agent override replaces the global scalar instead of falling back to it, the emulation could diverge for agents lacking catch-all patterns. In this repo all agent front matters declare catch-alls and every forbidden/required probe fails closed either way.
findings_list.recommendation: Document the assumed merge semantics (defaults -> global -> agent, scalar-as-fallback) in the validator header or validate against an OpenCode fixture.

findings_list.evidence: Compound families like *;*git add*, *|*git add* can false-positive-deny benign read commands that contain a pipe plus the literal text (e.g. git log | grep 'git add'); deny direction is fail-safe and the guardrail is documented as defense-in-depth in the manifest. Arbitrary-code keyholders (build/backend/frontend) can still bypass pattern denies via bash -c/subshel/backticks; this is documented and bounded by can_run_arbitrary_code.
